skill.name: hairline-create
skill.description: Use when someone asks for a new Hairline figure, or runs /hairline-create with an idea. Draws one isometric line figure that answers the pointer, in the style and on the engine of @lucasmarkes/hairline, and hands it over as a single self-contained HTML file.
skill.summary: Create pointer-responsive isometric line figures as self-contained HTML, with structural validation and optional browser screenshot checks.
skill.author: lucasmarkes

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are benign JavaScript syntax, documentation, CSS, or intended local file operations. Automatic npm installation exposes the host to mutable dependencies and enabled lifecycle scripts, while browser inspection lacks network isolation. No evidence found of credential theft, malicious supplied figures, or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Automatic dependency installation can execute host code.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit installation consent, pin an exact reviewed dependency with a lockfile, and disable lifecycle scripts in a controlled cache.

remediation.issue: Text validation does not isolate browser execution.
remediation.suggestion: Block external and local network requests, disable service workers, and enforce a restrictive content policy during inspection. Document that validation is not a security sandbox.

content.value_statement: Interactive line illustrations require consistent geometry, motion, and visual checks. This skill guides concept selection, builds a standalone HTML figure, and checks its structure and appearance.
actual_capabilities: Offer two or three concepts describing an object, pointer response, and short readout.
Create rounded isometric figures using the supplied geometry, spring, tween, and pointer helpers.
Assemble the fixed engine, page template, and figure into one self-contained HTML file.
Check syntax, kernel integrity, template consistency, required interfaces, and prohibited figure patterns.
Capture eight browser views covering rest, pointer response, thumbnail size, slider endpoints, and both themes.
Report frame bounds, readouts, console errors, and whether drawings settle during browser inspection.
limitations: Figures must follow the fixed Hairline engine, ten style rules, 400 by 320 drawing frame, and 200-line source limit.
Automated validation requires Node; screenshot inspection also requires npm, Playwright, and a compatible browser.
The screenshot helper may download dependencies into a user cache; installation requires security review and controlled permissions.
Visual quality needs human inspection, and text validation does not guarantee security isolation.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Pointer Interaction
use_cases.description: Explore how a tray, stack, or field responds to pointer movement before adapting the interaction to a product.

use_cases.title: Build a Shareable Illustration
use_cases.description: Create a standalone HTML line figure with theme switching, an intensity slider, and no runtime external assets.

use_cases.title: Explain a Process Through an Object
use_cases.description: Translate a process into a recognizable physical metaphor with one gesture and a short readout.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest three Hairline concepts for [idea]. Describe each object, pointer response, and short readout. Wait for my choice before building.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: explore an idea before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hairline figure of [object] that [pointer action]. Use the supplied engine and page, then validate the HTML. Ask before installing dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: build a selected object and gesture.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Every State
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [figure file] using [answer point] and [edge points]. Capture the eight views, report failures, and inspect the sheet. Ask before installing dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: verify geometry and interaction across views.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Without Changing the Engine
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine [figure file] to [requested change]. Edit only the figure, preserve stable hit areas, rerun validation, and disclose unverified checks. Ask before installing dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: revise an existing figure within the fixed framework.

output_examples.input: Suggest a Hairline metaphor for a deployment pipeline.
output: Locks: stepped canal basins open in sequence from the selected lock; the readout names its stage.
Marble run: hovering slows rolling marbles so the selected ramp can be inspected.
Cabinet: nearby server blades slide outward as the pointer selects an update position.

output_examples.input: Build the supplied Riffle example and describe its interaction.
output_examples.output: A standalone HTML page shows eight cards in a rounded tray. The selected card rises, neighboring cards lean away, and the slider controls stagger timing.

output_examples.input: Describe the visual inspection deliverables for a completed figure.
output: A labeled PNG sheet compares eight states, including thumbnails, slider extremes, and dark and light themes.
The inspection reports frame bounds, readouts, console messages, and settling observations.
Unverified visual checks are disclosed when no browser is available.

best_practices: Choose one recognizable object, one pointer gesture, and a composed rest pose before writing the figure.
Keep the engine and page unchanged, and review dependency installation before running browser inspection.
Validate after every edit, inspect all eight views, and disclose any checks that could not be performed.
anti_patterns: Modify the engine or page template to work around a figure problem.
Add labels, icons, custom colors, or independent animation timers inside the drawing.
Treat a passing text validator as proof of visual quality or security isolation.

faq.question: What does the skill deliver?
faq.answer: It delivers one self-contained HTML figure. The workflow can also produce a labeled PNG inspection sheet when browser tooling is available.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The workflow requires access to local files and appropriate execution tools.

faq.question: Does the finished figure need a server?
faq.answer: No. The assembled page contains its engine and figure, with no runtime external assets. Open the HTML file directly in a browser.

faq.question: What is required for automated checks?
faq.answer: Node runs the builder and validator. Screenshot checks additionally need npm, playwright-core, and Chrome or Playwright Chromium.

faq.question: Can I change the engine or use a different style?
faq.answer: This workflow keeps the engine and page fixed. Figures follow rounded isometric geometry, a restricted stroke palette, and the ten Hairline rules.

faq.question: Does successful validation prove the figure is safe?
faq.answer: No. Text checks are not a security sandbox. Review npm installation and inspect untrusted figures in an isolated environment.
